+## Protected integration and explicit escrow decision
+
+PR #455 merged through the protected workflow as `d517d6ed12a0f9ed3929df124507c7f4b025d16d`.
+Independent approval covered head `6fbae058e23c989599116c629a80fe216505c1e4`; all 22 checks passed.
+The merged tree matches the checked synthetic merge. Final backend CI
+[35553494963](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/35553494963) reported
+3511 examples, zero failures and six pending entry points delegated to passing separate runtime
+scripts. Post-merge [formal verification](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/35555279829)
+and [social verification](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/35555279871) succeeded.
+The immutable image [build](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/35555279975) succeeded:
+`sha256:18cc762956c97d2530e67a4117d1f27348503a7bba4774c0ec0c0df3fa4a0ef6`.
+It was deployed to existing staging after a confirmed database volume snapshot
+`vs_AY5zPmV7Ky5hKDyD9DbgwG`. The deployment command completed successfully; this is not a
+production release. Vercel deployment 6560713779 and the exact-commit Cloudflare check succeeded.
+
+The user then explicitly resolved SYS-C06: **disable both unverified financial writes**.
+SYS-D07 is the justified scope addition. Production rollout is held until the corrective handlers,
+regressions, compatible recovery, independent review and fresh exact-image checks are complete.
+The previously eligible recovery binaries still contain the nominal writers and must not be used
+for a release containing this disablement. See [legacy-escrow.md](legacy-escrow.md) for boundaries,
+provenance, machine-checkable correspondence and open obligations. No mobile source change,
+financial transaction, migration, historical payment rewrite or production rollout accompanies
+this intermediate checkpoint.
+
+
+### Escrow correction verification checkpoint
+
+Corrective PR [#461](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/pull/461) adds the explicit user
+scope decision. Head `0c34b2c0abe5d2db557ad8ae57db34cddcbfbde7` passed the complete
+[PR CI](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/35558077063), including actual
+backend handler regression executions. The separate recovery image run
+[35558075245](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/35558075245) passed backend,
+repository, migration, API, mobile and UI checks but failed the WebKit recovery-dialog close check;
+no image was produced. This failed run is not release evidence. The same browser check passed in
+PR CI; an isolated failure is retained as a limitation, not claimed fixed by the escrow change.
+
+Concurrent protected main `3dd26e0fa8cab6405bc3105078a4ee651d43bbca` adds the approved
+single daily event schedule and incomplete-inventory rejection. It is integrated without changing
+migration registrations or resetting effective production discovery flags. Synthetic-merge formal
+CI correctly rejected stale inventory; discovery is regenerated for the integrated source.
+Recovery now checks the exact handler bodies in both target and candidate source blobs, addressing
+review feedback about squash/cherry-pick ancestry and also detecting later reintroduction of writes.
+Source/guard regressions passed 84 checks locally. Fresh exact-head CI, image build and independent
+approval remain mandatory before protected merge and production delivery.
+
+
+The subsequent integration also includes protected main `5b29fcf68768fce18acbc2424b733459909856d7`
+(PR #459, bounded public YouTube metadata validation), with no migration-manifest change. The exact
+mobile gitlink is now checked out in the isolated worktree, removing the local source-access gap;
+native/store verification remains open. Catalog authority CI identified the new `disabledEscrowWrites`
+source-contract array; its two requirement/handler/message bindings are explicitly classified as
+technical verification constants, with a specific reviewed decision rather than an audit exemption.
+The recovery delivery uses a standard merge commit, preserving a separately tested PR-head image
+as a compatible ancestor. Initial squash integrations with no compatible ancestor intentionally
+remain blocked; this audit does not relax that release protection.
+
+
+### Required recovery-dialog gate (SYS-D08)
+
+WebKit dismissal failed again in [731 PR CI](https://github.com/diegueins680/tdf-app/actions/runs/35561739455),
+this time in English. The saved trace from the preceding Spanish failure shows the URL's `recover`
+parameter removed after click while the modal remains visible beyond the unchanged eight-second
+assertion. This is the already documented intermittent recovery issue, not a financial-handler defect.
+It is a necessary release-gate dependency. The recovery Dialog now unmounts when closed, avoiding
+reliance on the exit transition to remove the modal. A new actual-component regression fails against
+the prior implementation and passes after the change; all 11 LoginPage component tests pass. Six
+isolated pre-change Mac WebKit runs passed, so they do not reproduce or invalidate the hosted Linux
+counterexamples. Fresh browser validation is required. No timeout, retry count, focus assertion,
+locale assertion or accessibility rule was weakened. This evidence is testing, not a formal UI proof.
+
+The recovery image for `7314245c17a1413df3d86ff5c0cf6dc78185ac78` was subsequently built successfully
+by run35561775443 (the image run's independent browser matrix passed). Index digest:
+`sha256:1b482a9dc538c7e0d41198a21fc87e225778e9d79d1614328efbb49e4f702920`;
+amd64 digest `sha256:5d1a5570e21feaf72e7cb4dbc0f92d06f05ee3a5dc6872c170220c1cbf4ebd5a`.
+Its correction source passed bounded event/social analysis and the source-derived arithmetic checks.
+This image is an intermediate staging candidate, not a claim of final merged production delivery.
+The attempted local full Stack build was interrupted (exit130) after integration changed its source;
+only hosted clean-revision backend checks supply the complete-backend result for this checkpoint.
+
+
+Review #461 identified a recovery correspondence gap: candidate images could keep unused safe
+function definitions while routing a financial endpoint to a different implementation. The source
+contract now checks each candidate's marketplace dispatch, API ordering and authenticated parent/root
+bindings together with the bodies. Negative controls exercise rerouting each financial operation,
+replacing either parent dispatcher and changing/reordering API alternatives. The actual recovery
+callback is also checked not to run for a rerouted candidate. The 24 focused route/recovery checks
+pass locally; no unrestricted call-graph or whole-program proof is claimed.

+# Disabled legacy escrow writes
+
+Authority: explicit user decision, 2026-09-20: “Disable the two unverified financial writes.”
+This resolves SYS-C06 for the current delivery, consistently with accepted
+[ADR 0101](../../docs/adr/0101-verified-payment-events.md). No current exception was approved.
+SYS-D07 adds these two real financial writers and safe release recovery to the finite audit scope.
+
+| ID | Current guarantee | Actual implementation |
+|---|---|---|
+| SYS-ESCROW-001 | POST `/service-marketplace/bookings` rejects decoded authenticated requests with 503 and no financial or booking mutations | `TDF.API.ServiceMarketplaceAPI` → `protectedServer` → `serviceMarketplaceServer` → `createServiceMarketplaceBooking` |
+| SYS-ESCROW-002 | POST `/service-marketplace/bookings/:bookingId/escrow/release` rejects decoded authenticated requests with 503 and no payout or other mutations | Same route composition → `releaseServiceMarketplaceEscrow` |
+| SYS-ESCROW-003 | Recovery of a release containing this disablement cannot restore either legacy writer | `scripts/production-release.mjs` preflight, snapshot compatibility and recovery guard |
+
+The response is unavailable until a separately approved verified escrow implementation exists.
+There is no admin bypass, provider-mode exception or configuration switch. Existing nominal rows
+remain historical records, not verified funds. This change makes no assertion that they represent
+real money. Ad/slot operations and completion remain outside these two disabled writes; completion
+is not payout authorization. No schema migration or historical-row rewrite is required.
+
+## Executable contract and correspondence
+
+Let `S` be the complete persistent state before the handler, `u` any authenticated principal,
+`r` any decoded request, and `E` any environment. For each disabled handler `h`:
+
+```
+run(h(u,r), E, S) = (Left HTTP503(message_h), S, [])
+```
+
+`[]` is the sequence of handler-generated IO effects. The permitted transition is a stuttering
+step on every persistent entity, including Payment, ServiceEscrow, Booking, ServiceOrder and slots.
+All pre-existing states are admitted, including inconsistent legacy rows and absent IDs; the
+guarantee does not rely on their validity. No progress-to-payment property is required: these
+operations are explicitly disabled. Termination of the local handler follows its constant error
+expression; network response delivery is an environment assumption, not a liveness guarantee.
+
+The executable source contract is `scripts/lib/legacy-escrow-contract.mjs`. It recognizes exactly
+the two constant `throwError err503` definitions, the complete service-marketplace dispatch and
+API ordering, and their position in the authenticated parent/root composition. Body or binding
+changes fail the gate; keeping unused safe definitions cannot admit a rerouted writer. The manual reduction
+argument uses the ReaderT/Servant Handler error semantics: neither function evaluates its two
+arguments, reads Env, lifts IO, nor calls persistence. This is a narrow source-correspondence check
+and manually inspected effect argument, **not a machine-checked proof of Haskell or the whole API**.
+The compiler, imports, monad instances, Servant routing/authentication, runtime and deployment are
+trusted; the checker is intentionally not a general Haskell parser.
+
+Hspec extracts the actual handlers from `serviceMarketplaceServer` and executes them with a poison
+Env. It covers five role combinations, boundary Int64 identifiers, absent records and repeated
+release requests (55 executions). Accessing Env fails the test. Source-contract negative controls
+detect injected environment access, IO, successful return, admin overrides, rerouted handlers,
+replaced parent/root dispatch and changed/reordered API alternatives. Recovery reads both Git
+blobs (`Server.hs` and `API.hs`) from the candidate, not from the current checkout.
+The tests establish those executions, not unrestricted implementation equivalence. Authentication,
+JSON decoding and capture parsing may reject earlier with their existing status codes; HTTP clients
+are not promised 503 before they reach these handlers. Ordinary request logging is outside the
+handler-generated IO boundary.
+
+Composition: both mutations are removed, so interleavings of these handlers add no financial
+effects or state changes. This does not prevent independent writers or operators from changing
+the database. Future escrow implementation, existing-data reconciliation, provider correctness,
+global accounting invariants and all other payment routes remain separate open obligations.
+
+## Recovery correspondence
+
+The actual production tool checks the exact Git source blobs of both the target and every
+recovery candidate with the executable handler contract, in addition to the existing identity
+ancestry and migration checksum constraints. It rejects a target or recovery revision whose recognized handler body, marketplace dispatch,
+API alternatives or authenticated parent binding changes. This remains required after squash/cherry-pick integration and
+also detects later reintroduction, unlike an ancestry-only marker. Missing Git blobs/history are
+tool failures, never compatibility. Preflight validates the supplied recovery image and each prior
+machine image; recovery rechecks source before mutation. The concrete counterexample
+`d517d6ed12a0f9ed3929df124507c7f4b025d16d` has identical migrations and identity protections but
+still permits nominal escrow; it is rejected. Tests cover actual Git blobs, all four combinations
+of identity/financial predicates, missing source, squash-equivalent source, reintroduced writes and safe-but-unused stubs with rerouted financial
+endpoints. The checker does not prove arbitrary Haskell call graphs or all possible duplicate
+routes elsewhere; compiler/import/Servant semantics and reviewed surrounding application wiring
+remain in the trusted boundary.
+Current CI uses full history where actual historical blobs are regression inputs. Use the current
+guarded release tool; the contract does not control independent manual Fly operations.
+
+## Reproduce
+
+```
+node --test scripts/__tests__/legacy-escrow-contract.test.mjs scripts/__tests__/provider-rollback.test.mjs
+cd tdf-hq
+stack test --test-arguments='--match "disabled legacy service marketplace financial writes"'
+```
+
+The normal backend Hspec suite and formal specification CI run these checks. A relevant source
+change invalidates the correspondence argument and requires renewed review, checks and an exact
+image build. Required review, CI, compatible recovery, staging and production evidence remain
+delivery gates; committing this contract is not a deployment claim.
